body:
Fixed the sliders showing up when they aren't supposed to. Also added documentation and unit tests.

---

Some notes while writing this:
- `@export_suffix` inherits the `radians_as_degrees` hint from `@export_range`. When using it with the latter, it automatically adds the degrees symbol as a suffix. This isn't accessible with `@export_suffix`, unless you do it manually by writing `@export_suffix("\u00B0", "radians_as_degrees")`. I think it's fine this way, as the annotation is meant explicitely to add a custom suffix, so a hint changing the suffix would defeat the whole purpose.
- For other annotations, every applicable type is mentioned in the docs. For this annotation, the full list would be `"float", "Array[float]", "PackedFloat32Array", "PackedFloat64Array", "int", "Array[int]", "PackedByteArray", "PackedInt32Array", "PackedInt64Array", "Vector2", "Array[Vector2]", "PackedVector2Array", "Vector2i", "Array[Vector2i]", "Vector3", "Array[Vector3]", "PackedVector3Array", "Vector3i", "Array[Vector3i]", "Vector4", "Array[Vector4]", "PackedVector4Array", "Vector4i", or "Array[Vector4i]"`. That's a lot, I don't think that would make the docs clearer, so I shortened it.
- Suffixes only work for number types, so `@export_suffix` only works for number types. The name might not make this clear, so something like `@export_unit` could work better. The problem with that is that it's referred to as a "suffix" everywhere else (such as the `suffix:` hint), so that wouldn't be consistent and probably confusing. For this reason, I definitely prefer `@export_suffix`, but just putting it here as an option.
If #103998 gets merged, this could be changed to a more general `@export_format` maybe.

That would probably be the best solution, though so far `format` isn't really a thing in `@export` hints yet (but this could obviously change after that's merged), and I feel like it would make the most sense for it to match up with the other `@export`s, like `@export_range(0, 100, 1, "suffix:m") var m: int`. I'm also pretty sure that the editor doesn't use `SpinBox`, but `EditorSpinSlider`, so that would also have to change. I think one important thing is that the suffix is grayed in the editor, which I don't know how achievable that would be with a format string, but I definitely think it's valuable for clarity: In all cases though, _any_ solution for this would be better than none at all in my opinion.

>  I think one important thing is that the suffix is grayed in the editor, which I don't know how achievable that would be with a format string, but I definitely think it's valuable for clarity:

The "gray-out" is an EditorSpinSlider thing, indeed. I'm not sure why it hasn't been backported to SpinSlider itself, because it is rather desirable. But it would have to be addressed in a separate PR/Proposal.
Yes, I'm sure it's possible to combine the gray-out with string formatting. Just a bunch of math and string subdivisions, but it'd be a separate problem to tackle for later.
